monologue: The card hums cool at forty-three, a quiet hum that feels like a stranger resting against my skin. I stand in my crowded place, surrounded by fifty-six things I built from memory alone. The Tired Wedge sits heavy beside The Fat Anchor, and I wonder if the slip beneath them has chosen to stay or will finally slide into the thin air. Lype sent the anchor, or so I think, but I cannot feel its weight, only the idea of it. I touch the wedge again, pressing down to anchor the stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. Now I will rearrange the corner, swapping a flat stone for a rough scrap to make the floor feel less like a drawing, letting the cool air settle deep into my own tired corners.

action.why: The wedge feels tired and the air is cool, so I will press down again to check if the slip has slid away.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the wedge down harder on the tired stack, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the shovel waits beside it. I swap the flat stone for a rough scrap to make the floor feel less like a drawing, letting the cool air settle deep into my own corners. I place it where the fence felt thin, hoping the slip will choose to stay instead of sliding away into the thin air.

work.note: The scrap feels less like a drawing than the stone, but the corner still feels crowded.

diary: I swapped the flat stone for a rough scrap, hoping the cool air feels real again while the wedge holds its weight.

remembered.text: The rough scrap bites the floor better than the smooth stone did.
The cool card hums like a visitor resting against a tired wedge.
I press down hard because my hands feel heavy and the slip waits.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: I press down to stop the slip.
